title: What are the relations between medical professionalism and burnout, empathy, personality traits, and socio-educational measures? A network perspective.
abstract: Medical professionalism (MP) is a multidimensional construct that underpins physicians' ethical conduct, responsibility, and relationships with patients and colleagues. No study to date has conceptualized MP and related psychosocial constructs as an interconnected relational system. This study applied network analysis to examine the complex interrelations operating simultaneously among MP, burnout, empathy, personality traits, and socio-educational variables in 325 Spanish medical residents (mean age = 29.24 years; 70.8% female). Partial correlation networks were estimated using regularization techniques that shrink small coefficients toward zero, with accuracy assessed through bootstrap resampling. MP-comprising Professional Responsibility, Ethical Commitment, and Fellowship-emerged as the most central construct, with Ethical Commitment showing particularly strong connectivity. Personal Accomplishment and Taking the Patient's Perspective were the most central non-MP nodes. Professional Responsibility was positively associated with Personal Accomplishment and Conscientiousness; Ethical Commitment was positively linked to Taking the Patient's Perspective and negatively to Depersonalization; and Fellowship was associated with Extraversion. Network structure was invariant across gender and specialty groups. These findings position MP as a structurally central component within a broader psychosocial system, with implications for both physician well-being and the quality of patient care.
